headline: Southborough advanced a major Neary School addition-renovation design, navigated tight FY28 budget and capital planning, and debated key Special Town Meeting funding articles.
synopsis: In October, town officials focused heavily on long-range school and capital planning alongside preparations for Special Town Meeting. The Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance a comprehensive addition and renovation design for Neary School after learning a lower-cost upgrade would fund minimal repairs, while the School Committee reported an expected $2 million surplus from the Neary roof project. Departments submitted preliminary FY28 budgets under structural deficit warnings, and the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began reviewing $2.15 million in capital requests and up to $49 million in potential borrowing. The Community Preservation Committee advanced contentious funding articles for the Peninsula Trail footbridge and golf course irrigation to Special Town Meeting. Meanwhile, the Planning Board approved commercial site modifications along Route 9 while extending its Costco decision deadline to December, and the Zoning Board of Appeals advanced Chapter 40A compliance amendments while pausing local two-family zoning efforts.

top_items.title: Neary School addition-renovation option advances to schematic design
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted 4-0 to advance Option 3 for detailed design and cost modeling. Architects found a smaller $15 million upgrade would leave only $5.8 million for repairs after meeting code requirements.
top_items.body: After Tappé Architects revealed that a proposed $15 million base upgrade would be largely consumed by soft costs, code-mandated fire sprinklers, and ADA accessibility work—leaving just $5.8 million for actual repairs—the Elementary School Building Committee voted to pursue Option 3. This comprehensive addition and renovation plan will undergo schematic design and granular site cost modeling, including septic, parking, and educational spaces, targeting an anticipated spring 2027 Town Meeting vote.

top_items.title: Neary roof project yields $2M surplus; teacher contract amended
top_items.why: The School Committee learned the Neary roof project will return nearly $2 million in unused borrowing to the town. The committee also voted unanimously to align teacher salaries with Algonquin Regional High School starting in 2027.
top_items.body: District officials announced that the Neary Elementary School roof replacement is nearing 90 percent completion well under budget, enabling the district to return roughly $2 million of its $4.5 million Town Meeting borrowing authorization. In open session following negotiations, the School Committee also approved amendments to Articles 22 and 29 of the STA Unit A contract, adjusting retirement incentives and syncing Southborough's teacher salary schedule with Algonquin beginning July 1, 2027.

top_items.title: CIPC vets $2.15M capital requests and $49M borrowing outlook
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began vetting FY28 department submissions amid warnings of a $2 million structural operating deficit. School projects, fleet replacements, and infrastructure dominate initial requests.
top_items.body: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee reviewed FY28 submissions that include $2.15 million in potential direct appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable projects, heavily driven by school proposals. As municipal departments model level-service versus level-funded scenarios to address an operating deficit exceeding $2 million, the committee scheduled presentations from department heads and called for joint sessions with the Select Board and Advisory Committee to establish the town's debt capacity.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail footbridge article sent to Town Meeting without cuts
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to submit the $217,318 CPA funding request for the Route 30 pedestrian bridge as drafted. The Trails Committee dropped plans for a floor amendment reducing contingency funding.
top_items.body: Despite unfavorable recommendations from the Select Board and Advisory Committee, the Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send Article 4 to the Special Town Meeting warrant without cutting the $217,318 CPA appropriation. The Trails Committee abandoned a fallback proposal to strip out contingency money, deciding to present the full $428,550 bridge project and its safety benefits along Route 30 to voters directly.

top_items.title: Costco review extended to December; Route 9 site plans approved
top_items.why: The Planning Board extended its Costco decision deadline to December 18 while traffic peer reviews finish. The board also approved site plan modifications for 22 and 154 Turnpike Road.
top_items.body: With town peer reviews on traffic and stormwater still in progress, the Planning Board voted 5-0 to extend the statutory decision deadline for the proposed Costco at 21 Coslin Drive to December 18, 2026, scheduling a dedicated hearing for November 2. At the same meeting, the board approved modifications for the driving range at 22 Turnpike Road and the Chase Bank location at 154 Turnpike Road, placing conditions on outdoor lighting warmth and timer controls.

top_items.title: ZBA pauses two-family rezoning, advances state Zoning Act updates
top_items.why: Following the defeat of the two-family dwelling warrant article at Town Meeting, the ZBA agreed to await state legislation rather than draft another local amendment. The board also advanced Chapter 40A conformance updates.
top_items.body: After the two-family zoning article won a simple majority but fell short of the two-thirds threshold at Town Meeting, the Zoning Board of Appeals reached consensus to pause local efforts and monitor pending state legislation. The board also approved the withdrawal without prejudice of an occupancy appeal at 42-44 Central Street following state board intervention, and prepared updates to align local bylaws with state Chapter 40A revisions for the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Wastewater committee explores Zone C discharge and site analysis
top_items.why: State regulators confirmed wastewater discharge permitting is legally viable in Zone C of the reservoir watershed. The committee voted 6-0 to partner with Artefacts AI for pro bono parcel mapping.
top_items.body: The Wastewater Study Committee reported that Massachusetts DEP confirmed wastewater discharge permitting in Zone C of the Sudbury Reservoir watershed is feasible, though subject to strict treatment standards. To identify potential leaching sites of 15 to 20 acres along Route 9, the committee approved a pro bono partnership with Artefacts AI to conduct spatial analysis of town parcels ahead of planned District Improvement Financing.
